next_item_hypothesis: A demonstrated train-only failure pattern is directional next-item behavior: 314605 of 339519 observed transitions have no observed reverse event, with mean next-item entropy 4.844072338042215 bits. A single flat nearest-code geometry may allocate scarce early residual codes poorly across such asymmetric transition neighborhoods, causing histories that lead to semantically related but directionally distinct next items to share a coarse SID prefix. Hypothesis, not established causality: hyperbolic assignment distances on the same bounded latent vectors may better separate coarse branches while residual levels refine items. Stage2 emits one global three-token SID per item only; downstream T5 Stage3 ranks next items and is not part of this candidate.

math_definition.mechanism: Three-level residual vector quantization of content embeddings; only the nearest-code assignment distance changes between the curvature arm and its flat limit. There is no prefix Transformer, beam search, recommender loss, user bootstrap, graph signal, or Stage2 ranking.
math_definition.input_and_shapes: For train-split item set I_train with N items, content encoder output is E in R^{N x d_e}; frozen architecture maps E to Z in R^{N x 32}. Level codebooks C_l in R^{256 x 32}, l in {1,2,3}. Hard assignment tensors a_l in {0,...,255}^N; emitted SID for item i is (a_1i,a_2i,a_3i), globally fixed across users and contexts.
math_definition.curvature: c=1.0 in the hyperbolic arm; tau=1.0 for any distance-based soft reconstruction weighting (not used to alter hard assignments); epsilon=1e-5; arcosh argument clamp is max(u,1) in float64 before arcosh, with no positive offset. Stable arcosh(u)=log(u+sqrt((u-1)(u+1))) for u>=1, evaluated with the product form and log1p-compatible equivalent near one. All scored distances use the squared power.
math_definition.scored_distance: D^2(x,y)=d_c(x,y)^2=(1/c)*arcosh(1+2*c*||x-y||^2/((1-c*||x||^2)*(1-c*||y||^2)))^2. Its exact c->0 squared limit is 4*||x-y||^2; the unsquared distance tends to 2*||x-y||. The objective and assignments use squared distance in both arms.
math_definition.shared_domain_and_projection: Every vector entering a scored distance, including residuals and code vectors, is mapped by the same fixed radial projection P_R(v)=v*min(1,R/max(||v||,tiny)), with R=0.9, independent of arm. For c>0 the admissible projection radius is min(R,(1-epsilon)/sqrt(c)); at frozen c=1 this equals R. At c->0 the curvature-ball radius (1-epsilon)/sqrt(c) is undefined and is not evaluated; the flat arm applies P_R with the same fixed R. Feasible domain, coordinate convention, representation map, and projection are therefore identical in both arms. Domain policy: only vectors after P_R enter distance; require c*R^2<1 for positive-curvature parameter settings. For c->0 the denominator is interpreted by its continuous limit.
math_definition.c_dependent_rules_and_limits: The only c-dependent operation used is D^2 and the optional admissibility radius above. D^2 tends to 4*||x-y||^2, the corresponding unsquared distance tends to 2*||x-y||, and the exponential map Exp_0^c(v)=tanh(sqrt(c)||v||)*v/(sqrt(c)||v||) (defined as v at v=0) tends to the identity; this mechanism does not apply Exp, and its representation map is the identity in both arms. The radius (1-epsilon)/sqrt(c) is undefined at c=0, so the flat arm uses the shared fixed P_R rather than evaluating that radius. No other c-dependent transformation is used.
math_definition.assignment_target_distribution: For each item i and level l, define target tensor T_l in {0,1}^{N x 256} by T_l[i,k]=1[a_li=k], with a_li=argmin_{k in 0..255} D_c^2(v_li,P_R(C_lk)) and exact ties broken by smallest k. Each row is normalized by sum_k T_l[i,k]=1; targets are detached hard one-hot tensors and have no target for an empty item set (empty train set is an error). The target's dependence on current encoder/codebook parameters is broken by stop-gradient after deterministic hard assignment; it is not differentiated through.
math_definition.assignment_and_residual_order: For each item, initialize residual r_1i=P_R(z_i). At every level l in {1,2,3}, perform exactly: map v_li=r_li (identity map); project v_li=P_R(v_li); assign a_li using the stated one-hot target distribution; select q_li=P_R(C_l,a_li); subtract r_(l+1)i=P_R(r_li-q_li). Thus every residual update is map, project, assign, subtract, then project the new residual before its next scoring; no unprojected residual is scored. The flat arm executes the identical order and tensors with c=0 distance limit.
math_definition.target_and_loss: Let stop(a_l) be the nondifferentiable hard assignments computed from the current forward pass, detached before loss evaluation; this breaks target-depends-on-parameters circularity. Define Q_i=sum_{l=1}^3 P_R(C_l,a_li), Zp_i=P_R(z_i), and nonempty train-item set I_train. One scalar loss equation: L=(1/(N*32))*sum_{i in I_train}||Zp_i-Q_i||_2^2 + beta*(1/(3*N*32))*sum_{i in I_train}sum_{l=1}^3[||stop(P_R(r_li))-P_R(C_l,a_li)||_2^2 + gamma*||P_R(r_li)-stop(P_R(C_l,a_li))||_2^2]. Shapes: Zp,Q,r,C are 32-vectors per item/level; norms sum 32 coordinates; each displayed sum is a mean over its stated indices. beta=1.0 and gamma=1.0, frozen. The assignments are hard one-hot targets over 256 codes, normalized to sum to one per item and level; empty training-item set is an error and no loss is produced. The first commitment term updates code vectors toward detached residuals; the second updates encoder residuals toward detached selected code vectors. Reconstruction keeps the latent informative and prevents the all-items-same-code solution from minimizing the objective: content reconstruction error remains in the loss, with commitment anchoring both sides. No target distribution depends on a differentiable current parameter: hard assignments and the opposite-side commitment targets are detached.
math_definition.anti_collapse: math_definition.objective.anti_collapse is the content reconstruction term (1/(N*32))*sum_i ||P_R(z_i)-sum_l P_R(C_l,a_li)||^2, entering additively in L, plus the bidirectional stop-gradient commitment terms. It penalizes loss of item-specific latent information; constant SID assignment cannot minimize it unless the frozen content latents themselves are constant. No batch-composition or validation/test signal enters it.
math_definition.diagnostics_frozen_definitions: Use definitions verbatim: valid L1 positive hit rate is over 52855 frozen validation pairs (one positive plus ten negatives per anchor, seed 42, history[-1] -> target), share where anchor item's first SID token equals positive's first token. valid Hard-L1 ER=10*positive_hits/negative_hits with negative_hits counted identically over the ten negatives. level2_distinct_prefixes=|(k1,k2)| over all items. L3 collision is share of items whose (k1,k2,k3) is shared with another item. L3 refinement gain is mean over items of log2(|bucket(k1,k2)|/|bucket(k1,k2,k3)|). conditional G3 is mean over validation pairs of log2(p_hist(L3 target|anchor)/p_pref(L3 target|target prefix2)), where the train-transition history term is mixed into a Laplace-smoothed prior (alpha=1 over 256 codes). These validation diagnostics are evaluation only and are not training inputs.

hyperbolic_necessity: The observed directionality and entropy motivate testing a geometry that can allocate capacity to coarse asymmetric branches and finer nested residual distinctions; they do not prove hierarchy, negative curvature, or a causal gain. Negative curvature is a falsifiable inductive-bias hypothesis because a negatively curved metric can represent branching with increasing separation at shared coarse prefixes more economically than a flat metric. No claim that the supplied behavior evidence establishes curvature necessity.
euclidean_control: One implementation with c as the sole arm parameter: candidate c=1 and Euclidean control c->0. Both use identical content encoder and 32-D latent, identity representation map, fixed P_R projection, projected residuals/code vectors, codebooks in the same coordinates, assignments, reconstruction and commitment loss, optimizer, initialization, schedule, seeds, budget, and arithmetic path. The flat distance branch is the continuous limit of the same scored-distance function. The arms differ only in assignment metric formula, not Exp map, projection, representation, or coordinate conventions. No graph arm is used.
effect_site: Hard nearest-code assignments at each of the three residual levels; codebook geometry is optimized through the shared reconstruction-plus-commitment objective. Expected diagnostics: valid_l1_hard_er and valid_l1_positive_hit_rate; level2_distinct_prefixes; L3 collision, L3 refinement gain, and conditional G3. Stage3 test_R@10 is the downstream behavioral test; Stage2 does not rank.
real_trigger_measurement: Trigger is the frozen train-only observation that 314605/339519 directed transitions have no observed reverse event, alongside entropy 4.844072338042215 bits over the supplied train-only longest-prefix-per-user population. This identifies a measurable directional next-item failure hypothesis only, not an observed Stage2 failure, hierarchy proof, or causal result.
training_only_inputs: Content embeddings and item transitions from the train split only (train transitions are legal supervision under CLAUDE.md rule 16); no validation/test behavior, future events, prediction-time user context, or batch-composition signal is used for fitting, assignment targets, codebook updates, or loss. Validation is used only for the frozen Stage2 diagnostics; test is used only for the registered Stage3 evaluation.

stage2_diagnostics.name: valid_l1_hard_er
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: Per matched seed, compute the frozen valid Hard-L1 ER; register the seed's absolute value. Aggregate by the preregistered arithmetic mean across the same matched seeds; criterion is strict exceedance.

stage2_diagnostics.name: level2_distinct_prefixes
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: Count distinct (k1,k2) over all items for each matched seed; aggregate by arithmetic mean; criterion is strict exceedance.

stage2_diagnostics.name: L3_collision
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: Use the frozen item-share definition per matched seed; register candidate-minus-flat-control paired change, aggregate by arithmetic mean, and require strict decrease.

stage2_diagnostics.name: L3_refinement_gain
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: Use the frozen mean-log2 bucket refinement definition per matched seed; register candidate-minus-flat-control paired change, aggregate by arithmetic mean, and require strict increase.

stage2_diagnostics.name: conditional_G3
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: Use the frozen validation-pair conditional G3 definition per matched seed; register candidate-minus-flat-control paired change, aggregate by arithmetic mean, and require strict increase.

stage3_behavioral_test.seed_rule: Evaluate downstream T5 Stage3 test_R@10 under the already-frozen Stage3 protocol for paired matched seeds; register candidate-minus-flat-control change and aggregate by arithmetic mean; require strict increase. No Stage3 component is introduced into Stage2.

classification.falsified_if: all registered values are defined and finite, and (valid_l1_hard_er <= falsifier.stage2_diagnostics[0].minimum_effect OR level2_distinct_prefixes <= falsifier.stage2_diagnostics[1].minimum_effect OR L3_collision_change >= -falsifier.stage2_diagnostics[2].minimum_effect OR L3_refinement_gain_change <= falsifier.stage2_diagnostics[3].minimum_effect OR conditional_G3_change <= falsifier.stage2_diagnostics[4].minimum_effect OR test_R@10_change <= falsifier.stage3_behavioral_test.minimum_effect).
classification.passed_if: all registered values are defined and finite, valid_l1_hard_er > falsifier.stage2_diagnostics[0].minimum_effect AND level2_distinct_prefixes > falsifier.stage2_diagnostics[1].minimum_effect AND L3_collision_change < -falsifier.stage2_diagnostics[2].minimum_effect AND L3_refinement_gain_change > falsifier.stage2_diagnostics[3].minimum_effect AND conditional_G3_change > falsifier.stage2_diagnostics[4].minimum_effect AND test_R@10_change > falsifier.stage3_behavioral_test.minimum_effect.
classification.mixed_if: all registered values are defined and finite, and neither falsified_if nor passed_if holds; this includes a mix of favorable and unfavorable registered criteria. Any undefined/non-finite seed-wise or aggregated change, zero denominator, missing evaluation, or empty stratum is NULL; comparison with any NULL seed is inconclusive and classified NULL, not passed, falsified, or mixed.
